reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have doubled since August (from ~600/month in Jun-Jul to ~1200+/month in Aug-Sep, E-01), primarily because the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are built on reads marked ACTUAL that are themselves wrong — pointing to a fault in the billing import/read-acceptance step rather than in estimate substitution — while a tariff change has been ruled out (E-04, E-03). A smaller share of disputes (1240 of 3025) stems from ESTIMATED-read bills issued when manual-read route completion falls short of target (88% vs 95%, E-06); response-handling throughput is not the bottleneck since response times remain within SLA (E-02).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1200+/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-01) because the BV-17 high-consumption billing-import validation rule, deployed 2026-08-01 without unit scaling (E-14), misreads the raw register values of firmware-v4.2 AMI meters (which report in 0.1 m3 units since their 2026-06 rollout, E-13) as roughly 10x true consumption, wrongly rejecting valid AMI reads at billing import (1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts, E-12) and forcing those accounts onto disputed estimated bills instead of their accepted actual reads.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
